crit: 'we have selected thirteen data sets from UCI [3] which have different degrees of imbalance' (15 data sets after Letter and Splice were each split into two).
notes: SIGKDD Explorations 6(1), printed pages 20-29 (pdf p.1 = 20). minority_rule: the paper states a general rule ('we chose the class with fewer examples as the positive class, and collapsed the remainder', p.24 = smallest class vs rest) but Table 3 names the minority class of every data set in the 'Class (min., maj.)' column, and the text lists exceptions for Letter and Splice; coded 'explicit target listed' (adjudicator may prefer 'smallest class vs rest'). Class-merged: Letter-vowel uses 'all vowels' (several classes) as the positive class. Natural: Pima (1, 0), German (Bad, Good), Haberman (Die, Survive). Text says 'thirteen data sets' but Table 3 has 15 rows (Letter and Splice each used twice). Table 3 prints class percentages '(min., maj.)' and 'Majority Error', not an IR ratio or minority count. No data link; only the UCI repository URL in the references. Three methods are proposed (CNN+Tomek, Smote+Tomek, Smote+ENN); outcome rows record Smote+ENN (first in the data_key) with Smote+Tomek in the row notes; pruned ('yes') rows used. Typo in Table 4: German unpruned Smote+ENN '83.90(3.70))'. Figure 1 is a schematic and the artificial-data study is earlier work [18], so no Synthetic source.
